elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason, IBM will ..." — covers both expiry and termination, for any reason, with no request condition limited to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months"; the request condition operates after any expiry or termination and is not time-boxed to anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: "for up to six (6) months at IBM's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(b) within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return all Content to Customer" — the 30-day clock is anchored to expiry/termination, not to a request; "Content" is the Agreement's defined term for Customer-supplied information, software and data (Section 11.6).

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: "return all Content to Customer in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(c) after such return, delete all Content from its systems and certify such deletion to Customer in writing" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted trigger: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Six (6) months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, return all Content ... in a commonly used, machine-readable format".

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Section 3.5 addresses only accrued payment obligations, and 14.18 covers only processing instructions, so no exit, export or deletion mechanic existed anywhere.

The single inserted paragraph completes every preferred element (trigger, six months' assistance, then-current rates, 30-day return anchored to termination, machine-readable format, certified deletion after return), so the preferred level is position-complete and the fallback is met a fortiori.

Minimality holds: nothing existing was deleted or paraphrased, the retained accrued-payment sentence is untouched, and no survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or procedural boilerplate was added. Extending the trigger to "any Service Option Attachment" tracks the Agreement's own partial-termination structure expressly recognised in Section 3.5 and is therefore not surplus.

Intent is preserved: charges, payment timing and the Service Option Attachment mechanics survive without contradiction, and the drafter used the Agreement's defined term "Content" rather than introducing an undefined "Customer Data", so no dangling term or cross-reference results.

Minor note only (not a defect): if "Content" as defined in Section 11.6 is narrower than all data belonging to or processed for Customer, consider confirming on the next pass that the return/deletion obligation reaches all Customer-supplied and Customer-derived data held by IBM.
